<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:classical E}
		$\mathcal E=\bigcup_{I\in\mathrm{IP},\,\varepsilon\in\ell^1_+}\mathcal E(I,\varepsilon)$.
		\qed
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:classical E and BE}
		$\mathcal E=\mathcal{BE}$.
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->

\label{prp:simple relations}
		The following hold  for all $I\in\mathrm{IP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$ and $B\in\mathrm{BP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item\label{prp:simple relations:1} $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\forall\subseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)\subseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists\subseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa$,
			\item\label{prp:simple relations:2} $\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\forall\subseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(B)\subseteq\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\exists\subseteq\mathcal{BE}_\kappa$,
			\item\label{prp:simple relations:3} $\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\forall\subseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\forall$ and $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists\subseteq\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\exists$ and $\mathcal{E}_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal{BE}_\kappa$,
			\item\label{prp:simple relations:4} $\mathcal{E}_\kappa$ and $\mathcal{BE}_\kappa$ are ${\leq}\kappa$-complete ideals.\qed
		\end{enumerate}

\label{thm:BEk is not Ek}
		Let $\kappa$ be regular uncountable, then $\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\exists\nsubseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa$. Hence, $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists\subsetneq\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\exists$ and $\mathcal{E}_\kappa\subsetneq\mathcal{BE}_\kappa$.

\label{crl:Ekm is ideal}
		If $\kappa$ is successor, then let $I\in\mathrm{IP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$ be such that $\mathcal{E}_\kappa(J)\subseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)$ for all $J\in\mathrm{IP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$, then $\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)=\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists=\mathcal{E}_\kappa$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists$ is ${\leq}\kappa$-complete ideal when $\kappa$ is successor.\qed

\label{thm:EkA proper Ek(I)}
		Let $\kappa$ be regular uncountable. Then $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\forall\subsetneq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)$ for all $I\in\mathrm{IP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$, and $\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\forall\subsetneq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(B)$ for all $B\in\mathrm{BP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$.

<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Fix some $I\in\mathrm{IP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$, then \cref{thm:Ek(B) minmax}\,\ref{thm:Ek(B) minmax:1} shows that $\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)$ is not least, thus there is $J\in\mathrm{IP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$ with $\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)\nsubseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(J)$. It follows from this that $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\forall\subseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)\cap \mathcal{E}_\kappa(J)\subsetneq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)$. The same argument shows that $\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\forall\subsetneq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(B)$ for all $B\in\mathrm{BP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$.

<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:eveq equi}
		The following are equivalent for regular uncountable $\kappa$.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
			\item\label{eveq equi-1} The continuum function is eventually constant below $\kappa$.
			\item\label{eveq equi-2} The family $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists$ is closed under finite unions.
			\item\label{eveq equi-3} For every $B\in\mathrm{BP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$ there exists $I\in\mathrm{IP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$ with $\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)\subseteq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(B)$.
		\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-8 -->

		\begin{enumerate}

			\item $\mathcal{IAA}_\kappa=\mathcal{IA}_\kappa$, that is, the family of $\mathcal{IA}_\kappa$-additive sets is simply $\mathcal{IA}_\kappa$,
			\item If $\mathcal I_\kappa$ is ${<}\lambda$-complete, then so is $\mathcal{IA}_\kappa$,
			\item If $X+Y\in\mathcal I_\kappa$ for all $X,Y\in\mathcal I_\kappa$, then $\mathcal I_\kappa=\mathcal{IA}_\kappa$.\qed
		\end{enumerate}

<!-- thm-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:NAk subset BEkA}
		Let $\kappa$ be regular uncountable, then $\mathcal{NA}_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal{BE}_\kappa^\forall$.
<!-- end thm-12 -->

<!-- lmm-10: body_md -->
If $\kappa$ is successor, then $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\forall\subsetneq \mathcal{EA}_\kappa=\mathcal{E}_\kappa$.
<!-- end lmm-10 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
By \cref{crl:Ekm is ideal} we may choose $I\in\mathrm{IP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}$ with $\mathcal{E}_\kappa=\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)$, and since $\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)$ is additive, we see that $\mathcal{E}_\kappa=\mathcal{EA}_\kappa$. It then follows from \cref{thm:EkA proper Ek(I)} that $\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\forall\subsetneq\mathcal{E}_\kappa(I)=\mathcal{E}_\kappa$.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- thm-14: body_md -->
\label{EkE adds to everything}
		Let $\kappa$ be regular limit, then the following are equivalent:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item there exist $X,Y\in\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists$ for which $X+Y={}^{\kappa}2$.
			\item the continuum function is not eventually constant below $\kappa$,
		\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-14 -->

<!-- thm-21: body_md -->
\label{thm:add BEk and Ek are absolute}
		Assume $\kappa=\kappa^{<\kappa}$.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
			\item\label{thm:add BEk is absolute} $\operatorname{add}(\mathcal{BE}_\kappa)=\kappa^+$.
			\item\label{thm:cof BEk is absolute} $\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal{BE}_\kappa)=2^\kappa$.
			\item\label{thm:add Ek is absolute} If the continuum function is not eventually constant below $\kappa$, then $\operatorname{add}(\mathcal{E}_\kappa)=\kappa^+$.
			\item\label{thm:cof Ek is absolute} If the continuum function is not eventually constant below $\kappa$, then $\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal{E}_\kappa)=2^\kappa$.
		\end{enumerate}

<\kappa$. We call a set $B\subseteq{}^{\kappa}\kappa$ \emph{unbounded} if no $g\in{}^{\kappa}\kappa$ exists such that $f\leq^* g$ for all $f\in B$, and we call a set $D\subseteq{}^{\kappa}\kappa$ \emph{dominating} if every $f\in{}^{\kappa}\kappa$ has some $g\in D$ such that $f\leq^* g$. The \emph{bounding number} $\mathfrak b_\kappa$ is the least size of an unbounded subset of ${}^{\kappa}\kappa$ and the \emph{dominating number} $\mathfrak d_\kappa$ is the least size of a dominating subset of ${}^{\kappa}\kappa$.

<!-- dfn-10: body_md -->
Suppose that $\mathcal J $ is a subset of $\mathcal I $, then $\operatorname{add}(\mathcal J ,\mathcal I )$ denotes the least size of a set $J\subseteq\mathcal J $ such that $\bigcup J\notin \mathcal I $, and $\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal J ,\mathcal I )$ denotes the least size of a family $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal I $ such that every $J\in \mathcal J $ is contained in some $I\in\mathcal F$.
<!-- end dfn-10 -->
<!-- fct-2: body_md -->
If $\mathcal J \subseteq\mathcal K \subseteq\mathcal I $, then $\operatorname{add}(\mathcal K )\leq\operatorname{add}(\mathcal J ,\mathcal I )$ and $\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal K )\geq\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal J ,\mathcal I )$.\qed
<!-- end fct-2 -->

^{\leq

If $p,q\in\mathbb L\mathbbm{oc}_\kappa(B)$, then we define the ordering $q\leq p$ if and only if $\varphi_q\restriction \gamma_p=\varphi_p\restriction\gamma_p$ and $\gamma_q\geq \gamma_p$ and for each $\alpha\in\kappa\setminus\gamma_p$ we have $\varphi_q(\alpha)\supseteq\varphi_p(\alpha)$.

<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
That strategic ${<}\kappa$-closure is preserved under ${<}\kappa$-support iteration is well-known (see \cite[Proposition~A.1.6]{RoslanowskiShelah} for a proof). For ${<}\kappa^+$-c.c., note that there is a dense set $D$ of conditions $p\in\mathbb P_\mu$ such that for each $\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(p)$ there exists $s_\alpha\in\mathbf V$ for which $p\restriction\alpha\Vdash\text{``}\,\varphi_{p(\alpha)}\restriction\gamma_{p(\alpha)}=s_\alpha\,\text{''}$. Any two conditions $p,p'\in\mathbb L\mathbbm{oc}_\kappa(B)$ with the same stem $\varphi_p\restriction\gamma_p=\varphi_{p'}\restriction\gamma_{p'}$ are compatible, hence we can apply the sunflower lemma (i.e., the $\Delta$-system lemma).
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- thm-29: body_md -->
\label{thm:simple loc model}
		Let $\mathbf V\vDash\text{``}\,\mathsf{GCH}\,\text{''}$ and $\mu>\kappa$ be regular, then there exists a cardinal-preserving ${<}\kappa$-support iteration $\mathbb P_\mu$ of length $\mu$, where each of the iterands is (forced to be) of the form $\mathbb L\mathbbm{oc}_\kappa(B)$, such that $\Vdash_{\mathbb P_\mu}\text{``}\,\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{NA}_\kappa)=\mu\,\text{''}$.

<\kappa$.

		If $p,q\in\mathbb L\mathbbm{oc}_\kappa^\mathrm{new}$, then we let $q\leq p$ if and only if $s_p\subseteq s_q$ and $I^p\subseteq I^q$ and $F_p\subseteq F_q$, and for any $\alpha\in\operatorname{dom}(s_q\setminus s_p)$ and $f\in F_p$ we have $f\restriction I^q_\alpha\in s_q(\alpha)$.
<!-- end dfn-13 -->
<!-- lmm-15: body_md -->
$\mathbb L\mathbbm{oc}_\kappa^\mathrm{new}$ is ${<}\kappa$-closed and $(\kappa,{<}\kappa)$-centred.\qed
<!-- end lmm-15 -->

<!-- thm-30: body_md -->
Let $\mathbf V\vDash\text{``}\,\mathsf{GCH}\,\text{''}$ and let $\mu>\kappa$ be regular. Let $\mathbb C$ be the $\mu$-length ${<}\kappa$-support product of $\kappa$-Cohen forcing and let $\dot{\mathbb P}_\mu$ be a $\mathbb C$-name for the $\mu$-length ${<}\kappa$-support iteration such that for each $\alpha\in\mu$ we have $\Vdash_{\mathbb C\ast\dot{\mathbb P}_\alpha}\text{``}\,\dot{\mathbb Q}_\alpha=\mathbb L\mathbbm{oc}_\kappa^\mathrm{new}\,\text{''}$. Then 
		\[\Vdash_{\mathbb C\ast\dot{\mathbb P}_\mu}\text{``}\,\forall B\in\mathrm{BP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}(\kappa^+=\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{E}_\kappa(B))<\operatorname{cov}( 
	\def#1{} 
	\ifx#1\empty 
	\mathcal{M}_\kappa 
	\else 
	\mathcal{M}_\kappa 
	\def#1{m} 
	\defbig{big} 
	\defBig{Big} 
	\ifx#1\empty 
	\mathopen{}({})\mathclose{} 
	\else\ifx#1big 
	\mathopen{}\big({}\big)\mathclose{} 
	\else\ifx#1Big 
	\mathopen{}\Big({}\Big)\mathclose{} 
	\else 
	\mathopen{}\left(\right)\mathclose{} 
	\fi\fi\fi 
 
	\fi 
)=\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{E}_\kappa)=\mu=2^\kappa)\,\text{''}.\]
<!-- end thm-30 -->

)<\operatorname{cov}(

)=\mu=2^\kappa\,\text{''}$. It then follows from \cref{lmm:centred preservation} that $\mathbb P_\mu:=(\dot{\mathbb P}_\mu)^{[H]}$ is $(\kappa,{<}\kappa)$-centred in $\mathbf V[H]$. \cite[Definition 65]{vanderVlugt2025} defines a cardinal characteristic $\mathfrak{sup}_\kappa({\mathrel{\cancel{=^\infty}}})$, and from \cite[Lemma 79]{vanderVlugt2025} we know that $(\kappa,{<}\kappa)$-centred forcing notions preserve \mbox{$\mathfrak{sup}_\kappa({\mathrel{\cancel{=^\infty}}})=\kappa^+$}. Since $\mathfrak b_\kappa^{b,b}({\in^*})\leq \mathfrak{sup}_\kappa({\mathrel{\cancel{=^\infty}}})\leq \operatorname{non}( 
	\def#1{}

	\mathcal{M}_\kappa

)$, we may use \cref{cov Ek as a localisation number} to conclude that $\Vdash_{\mathbb C\ast\dot{\mathbb P}_\mu}\text{``}\,\forall B\in\mathrm{BP}_\kappa^\mathrm{lim}(\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{E}_\kappa(B))=\kappa^+)\,\text{''}$.
		
		Now, working in $\mathbf V[H]$, suppose that $\dot X$ is $\mathbb P_\mu$-name for a subset of ${}^{\kappa}2$ of size ${<}\mu$, then there is a stage $\gamma<\mu$ such that $\dot X$ is a $\mathbb P_\gamma$-name. But, as we discussed above, in the next stage of the iteration a slalom $\varphi_\mathrm{gen}$ is added such that $\dot X\subseteq 
	\def#1{}

	\ifx#1\empty

	\mathopen{}\Big[{\varphi_\mathrm{gen}}\Big]\mathclose{}

	\fi\fi\fi 
_*$, thus $\Vdash_{\mathbb P_\mu}\text{``}\,\dot X\in\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists\,\text{''}$. Consequently, $\Vdash_{\mathbb C\ast\dot{\mathbb P}_\mu}\text{``}\,\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists)=\mu\,\text{''}$ and thus the theorem follows from $\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{E}_\kappa^\exists)\leq\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{E}_\kappa)$.
